title: Adire indigo resist dyeing
summary: Adire is blue-and-white cloth made by Yoruba women of south-western Nigeria. Parts of the cloth are tied with raffia, stitched, or covered with cassava paste so that the indigo cannot reach them; when the cloth is washed and opened, pale circles, lines and shapes show on the deep blue ground.
howToPlay: Pick a shade of indigo and a shape from the tray under the cloth.
Touch a square to place that shape: it is repeated on the squares where the folded cloth would show it again.
Copy the small cloth shown above, then press Check.
rules: The cloth is treated as if folded in four and then in half, so each shape you place is copied to all its matching squares, up to seven partners.
A square counts only when its shape and its shade of indigo both match the target.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Adire is closely associated with the Egba people of Ogun State and the town of Abeokuta, with important work also in Ibadan and Osogbo. Patterns are named and are often passed from mother to daughter.
